solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticism at change of course

parts.note: to tack is to change a sailing boat's course by turning into the wind

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone has switched policy direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal assault on someone's work or views is fierce criticism.

clue.text: A couple of pence increase in value

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny, so two of them give PP
to raise something is to increase it

explanation.surface: A tiny price rise of two pennies adds to something's worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To value goods is to assess their worth, a synonym for estimating a price.

clue.text: Revealing Rossini's libretto?

parts.note: Rossini wrote the opera William Tell, so his hero is Tell
a libretto is the text or story of an opera, a tale

explanation.surface: Asks whether the words of a Rossini opera give something away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the libretto of William Tell; split it as the opera's hero plus the story it tells.
explanation.definitionFit: A giveaway sign that betrays a secret is described as revealing, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: A short cut for sailors

definitions.meaning: a ... cut is a very short haircut, named after rowing ...
the people who man a ship

explanation.surface: A quick route offered to seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company of seamen, and the close-cropped haircut that bears the same name.

clue.text: Burly but brainless band

parts.note: thick is informal for stupid
a set is a group or band of people

explanation.surface: A musical group whose members are strong but dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Burly and stocky both describe a heavily built, solid body.

clue.text: An angel-fish? Gracious!

definitions.meaning: a mackerel that is holy, as an angel would be, said humorously

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at seeing an angelfish.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment, and a whimsical picture of a saintly mackerel as an angelic fish.

clue.text: The Joker in the pack?

parts.note: the joker is one of a pack of playing ..., and an amusing, eccentric person is also called by the same word

explanation.definitionFit: A wag or comedian is informally called this, and the joker is one in a deck.

clue.text: Ring up a number of soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ten is a number
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A command to telephone a group of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal engraved on a finger ring, used to stamp documents.

clue.text: It doubles up with an old master

indicators.note: in a down clue the doubled word is read upwards
doubles tells us to write the word it twice

explanation.surface: Something teams up with a classic painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the word to be written twice and then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance painter is one of the great old masters.

clue.text: The favourite's all in — made to carry a big weight

definitions.text: made to carry a big weight

indicators.note: the favourite's ... in says the next word is placed inside it

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A racing favourite is weighted heavily by the handicapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden platform for stacking heavy goods so a forklift can move the load.

clue.text: Perfect exam performance — or just fair?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a test result was flawless or merely middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, every answer correct; idiomatically, just satisfactory or acceptable.

clue.text: Forsake television for toy

parts.note: to jack in is informal British for giving something up
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: Advice to give up TV in favour of playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's novelty in which a figure springs out of a case when the lid opens.

clue.text: Star-strewn university faculty

indicators.note: strewn means scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A college department decorated with stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanities faculty of a university covers subjects like history and literature.

clue.text: Royal Marines seen in the sea inlet — but not all there

indicators.note: the marines are seen in the inlet, so they go inside it

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the sea

explanation.surface: Commandos landing in a bay are a little crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for mad, and 'not all there' is an idiom for mentally lacking.

clue.text: Big star gave trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are disturbed and put out of order

explanation.surface: A celebrity caused problems.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the brightest stars in the night sky, in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Boat causes waters to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: pools are bodies of water

explanation.surface: A vessel makes the water level climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A small single-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Counterfoils seen in the ashtray

definitions.meaning: the retained parts of tickets or cheques
cigarette ends left in an ashtray

explanation.surface: Ticket remnants dumped in an ashtray.
explanation.definitionFit: The leftover short ends of cheques and of cigarettes share one name.

clue.text: US capital gives Sally a ticket — free!

indicators.note: free here means loose, so the letters are released into a new order

explanation.surface: An American city hands Sally a complimentary ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Utah is a US capital.

clue.text: Grade the produce harvested

indicators.note: to produce is to make something, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Sorting the crops that were picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' reads as a noun for crops, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops that have been harvested have been collected in.

clue.text: Academic bosses admit financial liability

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the studs take the debt inside

parts.note: bosses are raised studs on a surface
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: University managers confess to money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bosses' suggests managers; here it means knobs or studs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookish and given to scholarship, which is what academic means as an adjective.

clue.text: Token expletive in defiant response

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games
blast is a mild oath

explanation.surface: A curse offered as a gesture of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous retort or rebuttal made against an attack.

clue.text: Wild animal seen in the Philippines

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: An untamed beast spotted in Southeast Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the Philippines, which a visitor would see there.

clue.text: Providing back up when company is a failure

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read backwards, going up

parts.note: if means providing that
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A firm collapses unless someone gives support.
explanation.definitionFit: A humiliating flop or complete disaster.

clue.text: Surrounded by a number in support

indicators.note: in places the number inside the word for support

parts.note: aid is help or support
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Encircled by digits that prop something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning in the middle of, among.

clue.text: Main source of inspiration in cook

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the cook

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: the source is where something starts, so take the opening letter

explanation.surface: A kitchen worker draws chiefly on one muse.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal or foremost, as in the chief reason.

clue.text: Slough outbuilding

definitions.meaning: to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A hut in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town west of London, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off skin, and a small garden hut, share one spelling.

clue.text: Examination of the mouth?

parts.note: suggests a dentist's check-up, but means a spoken test

explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test uses the mouth, and the word describes anything relating to it.

clue.text: Start work in French — at this university?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
en is French for in

explanation.surface: Beginning a job in French at a particular college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at this university?' adds a nod to Britain's Open University, the distance-learning institution.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin proceedings, as when one opens a meeting.

clue.text: Fashionable writer will make his mark

parts.note: in means in fashion
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A trendy author will become famous.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave or write words on a surface is literally to leave one's mark.

clue.text: Poor to riot in Portuguese city

indicators.note: to riot is to run wild, so the letters break into disorder

explanation.surface: Impoverished people rise up in a Portuguese town.
explanation.definitionFit: The English name for Porto, the port-wine city in northern Portugal.

clue.text: A stroke of the worst misfortune?

definitions.text: A stroke of the worst misfortune?

parts.words: A stroke of the worst misfortune?
parts.note: plays on 'stroke of bad luck' while meaning a medical stroke

explanation.definitionFit: An old medical term for a stroke, a sudden loss of consciousness caused by a brain bleed.

clue.text: Positive points in article do back different points

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: back means the word do is read in reverse

parts.note: E and S are two different compass points

explanation.surface: A list of plus points in a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrodes with positive charge, toward which anions travel.
